title: Prove sharp theta order for broad Gaussian edge inverses (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped analytic proof with exact finite corroboration. The broad Gaussian inverse at a phase-cell edge has sharp order Theta_alpha(theta^(-1/2)) for fixed alpha, answering the matching-lower-estimate question left by JoyboyBrian's merged #5103.

```text
K[k,i] = alpha^-1 exp(-pi/alpha^2 (i-k/rho-c)^2)
rho=1+theta, c=1/(2rho), theta(N-1)<=1

||K^-1||_2 >= alpha m exp(-pi theta (2m-1)^2/(alpha^2 rho))
for every integer m>=1 with 2m<=N

0<theta<=1/16, N>=2 floor(1/(2 sqrt(theta)))
  => ||K^-1||_2 >= (alpha/4) exp(-pi/alpha^2) theta^(-1/2)
```

The new proof preserves a positive term of the checkerboard finite q-LDU inverse through the exact diagonal gauges, then applies an explicit alternating test vector to an m by m boundary rectangle. Combining this lower estimate with #5103's cited upper theorem proves matching order. The proposed sharp leading coefficient in Ryanson Jonathan's #4435 remains open. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit JoyboyBrian #5103 for the upper theorem and lower-bound question, Ryanson Jonathan #4408/#4435 for the scaling observation and formal prediction, Jose Manuel/jmbarrancoml #4193 for the finite inverse estimate, Vlado Vojdanovski and the retained #1673 Gaussian/q-LDU lineage, Cinna Davis's later caller, and the classical q-binomial identities. Predecessor code, numerical tables and operator replays are not the deliverable.

## Evidence

Before: a rigorous theta^(-1/2) upper theorem with a matching lower estimate explicitly open. After: the quantified lower estimate above proves that order is necessary on the stated boundary sections.

The independent exact verifier passes 36 rational Gaussian matrices, 416 inverse-entry checks, 50 rectangle/test-vector checks, 520 rational exponent checks, 1,009 floor cases and nine boundary/sign/overstatement controls. Rational fixtures use the more general positive-exponent Gaussian family; the written proof specializes to the original pi/alpha^2 kernel. At the actual alpha=3, theta=1/400, N=400 fixture, a rational certificate gives a new inverse-norm lower bound exceeding 109/5. This is not its exact norm.

Using CPython 3.12.15 and only the standard library, both registered commands pass locally. Warning-strict normal and optimized direct runs take 0.79 and 0.80 seconds; read-only Git-free export runs take 0.80 and 0.81 seconds. The registered runner, six-file committed-byte/source-history preflight and official export integrity pass at head c16d2fc11e2891bec18d6a9fa3f8ed4e743de6b2. Normal and optimized export reports agree, and the generated external receipt binds all six package files by SHA256.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem fixes beta_0=-1/2 and needs a section containing a theta^(-1/2) boundary window. It does not give this lower order for tiny sections or sections separated from the cell edges. Its alpha-dependent constant is coarse; no sharp leading coefficient or matching growing-alpha law is proved.

The written argument carries the universal quantifiers. Finite exact checks corroborate it. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No Lean, Docker, predecessor scientific replay or selected operator replay was run. Coefficient preparation, rounded inverse application, circuit prefixes, source access, restoration, storage/tape, native implementation, compiler and outer integer recovery remain unpriced. This is not a supplier admission or complete multiplication theorem. Every registered package command ran locally; none is deferred to CI.

## Open next questions

- Recover #4435's sharp leading coefficient with a uniform boundary remainder, including a growing-alpha regime. Start with more positive inverse terms and optimized boundary test vectors; a comparably sharp upper estimate remains necessary.
- Bind one complete rounded Gaussian caller and retain its coefficient, prefix, restoration, movement and storage costs before changing its numerical guards.

## Related open work

No open PR studying this broad phase-cell inverse lower-order quantity was found in the live list and complete cached PR-body coverage. #5103, #4435, #4408 and #4193 are merged predecessors. Their upper estimates, formal prediction and constant-shift results are cited at their stated scopes; no additional computations were run to compare their reported numbers.

Completion refresh: this account has ten open PRs created since the advance CLAIM, including this PR. The nine others are #5145, #5146, #5148, #5149, #5151, #5152, #5153, #5154 and #5155. None studies this broad phase-cell inverse-norm quantity. Two adjacent precision results have different hypotheses and quantities:

- #5145 proves an optimal scalar Neumann truncation coefficient with its contraction and prefactor granted. This proves an inverse-norm lower order and does not compare that scalar tail or its constants.
- #5153 proves an endpoint-conditioned coefficient-rounding guard for finite words. This concerns exact completed Gaussian conditioning and does not establish a rounding guard or compare its constants.
